headline: EQSweep app fine-tunes Pixel Buds sound quality with test tones
summary: This free Android app helps you identify and fix frequency gaps in your headphones by listening to test tones, rather than guessing with sliders.
details: Google Pixel Buds are praised for their fit and discreet design, but their default sound profile can be too treble-forward for some users. While Google's built-in equalizer offers some adjustments, it lacks the granular control needed for a truly personalized audio experience.

Enter EQSweep, a free, community-built Android application that offers a novel approach to headphone equalization. Instead of relying on presets or standard graphic sliders, EQSweep guides users through identifying specific frequency issues by listening to test tones.

The app plays a sweeping sine wave across the audible frequency range. By maintaining consistent volume, users can pinpoint frequencies that sound unusually loud or quiet, indicating peaks or dips in the headphone's response.

Once problem areas are identified, EQSweep allows users to create custom equalizer bands. You can define the start and end points of a frequency range, adjust its gain (volume), and width, enabling precise tuning to achieve a balanced sound.

The process involves a full frequency sweep, with users marking sections that stand out. This granular control allows for targeted adjustments, such as taming excessive treble or boosting bass, without affecting a wide range of frequencies.

Users can create up to 10 custom bands and save multiple presets, allowing for on-the-fly sound adjustments to suit different music genres or listening preferences. This offers a level of customization previously unavailable to Pixel Buds users.
